name: Tomatillo
grown_as: A tender annual grown like a tomato, in a greenhouse or warm spot. Also sold as Physalis ixocarpa. Fruit green or purple by variety: drawn green. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A sprawling, branching bushy plant 60 cm to 1.2 m, wider than tall, with smooth angled stems. Needs a stake or cage.

leaf.margin: A few coarse, irregular, uneven teeth, or nearly entire

flower.form: An open, shallow wheel or bowl, slightly nodding
flower.petals: Five, joined, with five shallow broad lobes
flower.colour: Bright yellow with five dark purple-brown blotches in the throat
flower.behind: A small green calyx with five teeth, which grows after flowering into the papery husk
flower.carried: Singly on short stalks from the leaf joints, facing out or down

fruit: A round berry 3 to 6 cm inside a papery husk (the swollen calyx), the husk pale green, often purple-veined, with five or ten ridges, hanging from the stems like small lanterns. The fruit fills and often splits the husk when ripe. Fruit green to yellow-green (purple in some), sticky under the husk. Seeds tiny, flat, pale buff.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves on a thin stem; first true leaves simple, oval and toothed.
winter: Nothing: killed by frost. Self-sown seedlings may come next year.

bloom: five dark blotches in the throat
young: simple pointed leaves with a few coarse teeth
flower: yellow bowl flowers with dark blotches in the throat
crop: green papery husks hanging like lanterns
round green fruit filling or splitting the husk

look_alikes: Cape gooseberry (Physalis peruviana) is soft-hairy with a smaller orange fruit in a brown husk that it does not fill. Chinese lanterns have white flowers and bright orange husks.
